AUTHOR: Francisco
TITLE: High-resolution, non-invasive animal tracking and reconstruction of local environment in aquatic ecosystems
SPECIES: Conger conger; Mullus surmuletus, Diplodus vulgaris; Lamprologus callipterus
DATA: Own snorkel/SCUBA stereo and multi-camera videos: 'single', 'mixed', 'school' datasets plus 'accuracy' calibration-wand dataset
V_EV: Methods: 'The remaining datasets were collected via SCUBA (5-8 m) with either multi or stereo camera set-ups'
D_EV: no statement found (Methods only: 'we trained Mask R-CNN models on small subsets of labeled video frames ... visually confirmed with predictions on validation datasets')
R_EV: Methods: 'we trained Mask R-CNN models on small subsets of labeled video frames' per dataset; no evaluation outside each dataset
C_EV: Methods: 'filtering for linear motion over a short time window, reducing later quality control and manual track identification' and GUI for 'manual track corrections'
E_EV: Results/Fig. 3: 'Trajectories were successfully obtained from large groups (school), small groups (mixed) and single individuals (single).'
ARCH: Mask R-CNN (matterport) + COLMAP Structure-from-Motion + triangulation; nearest-neighbour/Hungarian track assignment
METR: Reconstruction RMSE (cm), reprojection error (px), calibration-wand tracking error (cm)
NOTE: Text file is the bioRxiv preprint (different title: 'High-resolution animal tracking with integration of environmental information in aquatic systems') of the Movement Ecology paper; coded from it. INCL borderline: no fish detection metrics, only geometric accuracy (reprojection errors on fish tracks; wand-length error on non-fish 'accuracy' dataset); detection quality only 'visually confirmed'. C5 credited for manual track correction/identification (could be judged insufficient -> C_ALL NR). E1=행동 (3D trajectories/poses shown) with no ecological comparison; wand known-length check is not a fish ecological reference. NIMG = 171+80+160 fish training frames (plus 73 wand frames).
AUTHORS_FULL: Francisco, FA; Nührenberg, P; Jordan, A
